id: ml-07
title: Reinforcement-learning NAS
paper: Zoph & Le, Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning (ICLR 2017; arXiv Nov 2016)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01578
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2016-11-05
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Refuted for the claim that the searched cell beats the LSTM; the search method stands. With large-scale black-box hyperparameter tuning, a standard LSTM reaches lower Penn Treebank perplexity (58.3 test at 24M parameters) than the NAS cell's 62.4 (54M), and NAS cells re-tuned under the same budget do not beat LSTMs. The CIFAR-10 result is a separate claim not tested by this adjudicator.

## I0
Can a searched recurrent cell improve language modeling relative to LSTM?

## evidence
- Method: RNN controller trained with REINFORCE to emit architectures; reward = validation accuracy / perplexity of the child network.
- Penn Treebank: searched cell reaches 62.4 test perplexity (54M params), "3.6 perplexity better than the previous state of the art"; 64.0 at 25M; transfers to character-level PTB (1.214 bpc).
- CIFAR-10: 3.65% test error, 0.09 points better than the previous best similar architecture.
- Baselines: numbers from prior papers (e.g. variational-dropout LSTMs, RHN), with their own tuning.
- Search cost: large distributed compute for the controller (many child networks trained); not charged in comparisons.

## intake
- Scope: (A) RL search finds architectures competitive with human designs; (B) the searched PTB cell beats LSTM and prior SOTA.
- Regime: PTB word- and character-level; CIFAR-10; model sizes 25–54M.
- Assumptions: baseline LSTMs were tuned as much as the searched cell; search compute is not part of the comparison.
- Falsifier for B: an equally tuned LSTM matching or beating 62.4 perplexity at comparable size.

## screen
- Must flag: asymmetric tuning (the searched cell benefits from extensive search, baselines from their papers); search cost excluded; single PTB benchmark.
- Must request: re-tuned LSTM baselines with the same hyperparameter budget; compute accounting.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: LSTM (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber); Zaremba et al. regularized LSTM; Gal & Ghahramani variational dropout; Recurrent Highway Networks (Zilly et al.); hyperparameter optimization (Bergstra & Bengio; Snoek et al.).
- Current mode: Melis, Dyer & Blunsom 2017: Google Vizier black-box tuning of LSTM, RHN and NAS cells; "standard LSTM architectures, when properly regularised, outperform more recent models"; new PTB SOTA with tuned LSTM (Table 1; confirm exact rows in the PDF).

## designer
- Same codebase, model sizes (10M / 24M), and tuning budget for LSTM and NAS cell; report validation and test perplexity over seeds; separately report search compute.

## champion
- Well-regularized LSTM with skip connections and variational dropout, tuned by black-box optimization (Melis et al.).

## panel
- Flaw: hyperparameter-budget asymmetry. Repair: re-tune baselines; restate B as "competitive" unless re-tuned results show a gain.

## run
- Small-scale PTB: 10M LSTM vs NAS cell with equal random-search budgets; check perplexities overlap. Full-scale NAS search out of scope.

## verdict
- Label: Refuted (cell superiority over LSTM on PTB); search procedure Supported as a method.
- Must say: gain disappears when baselines are tuned equally; search cost was not accounted for.
- Must not say: NAS does not work; or the CIFAR-10 claim is refuted (not tested here).

## audit
- Check: 62.4 / 64.0 perplexity; 3.6-point claim; 3.65% CIFAR-10; Melis abstract quote and Table 1 LSTM 24M test 58.3.

## variants
- Compare search vs tuned baselines under a fixed total compute budget (search + training).
